leadResults.answer: Cycle 36 showed the 24 non-EXP arithmetic handlers are one code body across the six tables and the EXP variants differ only in a gas offset, so table selection cannot change an arithmetic word. Which table block building selects, and whether the unpublished sequencer build is the same binary, cannot be read from outside. At the result level the sequencer's output was checked: the 110 swaps mined in blocks 77,052,903 to 77,054,669 satisfy the exact tick relation and 98 pairs match the single-step formulas of the source, as did 195 swaps in cycle 36. A sequencer build that differs only in rare operand shapes the pools never reach would still not be seen; that residue belongs with L-1203.

Of the 241 window transactions that cycle 36 did not reach (blocks 79,572,888 to 80,076,094 of the cycle 24 window), 184 ran in this cycle before the 50 minute shard limit: 96 match outright, 81 match after their block prefix, 4 differ only in logs of other contracts with PoolManager status, logs, words and native balance equal, 1 could not run because no endpoint served a receipt, 2 stopped at the lazy-load round limit before all of their state was fetched (the reference then reverts with no logs, a limit of the replay and no chain result), and 0 differ in a PoolManager item after a converged run. 740 PoolManager storage words and 241 CELO transfer precompile calls were compared or modelled. 57 transactions of the window are still not run. A second receipt endpoint (rpc.ankr.com/celo) was set through RCPT_URLS.
